name: Learning from causal relationships in data
gist: Papers using causal reasoning to identify true cause-and-effect relationships in data, avoiding spurious correlations and enabling more reliable decision-making.
explain: A medical study finds that people who take vitamin supplements have lower heart disease rates. Does this mean supplements prevent disease? Or do health-conscious people take supplements and exercise more? The correlation between supplements and low disease exists, but the causation is unclear. Standard machine learning models learn correlations — they extract patterns that hold in the data. But correlation is not causation, and when you act on a false correlation, you waste resources or harm people. This subtheme tackles learning the true causal structure of data: what actually causes what.

The difficulty is that observations alone cannot determine causation. You can collect petabytes of data showing that rain tends to occur when the barometer drops, but the barometer drop does not cause rain — falling atmospheric pressure causes both. Without intervention, you cannot tell. Real causal reasoning requires understanding the underlying mechanisms. Additionally, causal relationships are often hidden or complex. Many variables influence each other: education affects income, but education quality depends on family wealth, and family wealth also affects income independently. Untangling these chains of causation is hard because you cannot run experiments on every human's life.

Researchers use causal graphical models — diagrams showing which variables directly influence which others — to reason about causation. They develop techniques to estimate causal effects from observational data by adjusting for confounding factors (variables that influence both cause and effect). They study when and how causal models can be inferred from data and assumptions. Some work uses structural assumptions about how variables relate (e.g., if A causes B and B causes C, then A indirectly influences C) to narrow down plausible causal structures. The field also applies these ideas to machine learning: training on causal relationships rather than spurious correlations leads to models that generalize better when the world changes, because the true causes remain stable even if surface patterns shift.

papers.title: ActiveCQ: Active Estimation of Causal Quantities
papers.contribution: Their framework significantly outperforms baselines, achieving substantial gains in sample efficiency across a variety of causal quantities through information gain and total variance reduction strategies.

papers.title: Causal Discovery in the Wild: A Voting-Theoretic Ensemble Approach
papers.contribution: Provides theoretically justified guidance on optimal ensemble design (number, competency, and diversity of experts) and demonstrates robustness and effectiveness on synthetic and real-world datasets.

papers.title: Distributional Equivalence in Linear Non-Gaussian Latent-Variable Cyclic Causal Models: Characterization and Learning
papers.contribution: This is the first equivalence characterization with latent variables in any parametric setting without structural assumptions, enabling the first structural-assumption-free causal discovery method.

papers.title: Efficient and Sharp Off-Policy Learning under Unobserved Confounding
papers.contribution: Achieves optimal confounding-robust policy selection with applications to healthcare and public policy, outperforming plug-in approaches.

papers.title: Frequency-Domain Better than Time-Domain for Causal Structure Recovery in Dynamical Systems on Networks
papers.contribution: Establishes that frequency domain provides distinct advantages for recovering Markov Equivalent Graphs in networks with dynamical dependencies through theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Journey to the Centre of Cluster: Harnessing Interior Nodes for A/B Testing under Network Interference
papers.contribution: Substantially reduces variance compared to classical network-aware estimators while using semi-supervised learning to address representativeness of interior nodes.

papers.title: Learning Dynamic Causal Graphs Under Parametric Uncertainty via Polynomial Chaos Expansions
papers.contribution: On a large-scale chemical reactor dataset, the framework learns dynamic causal structure with 90.9% F1-score, nearly doubling baseline performance and providing interpretable models of causal mechanism evolution.

papers.title: Learning Exposure Mapping Functions for Inferring Heterogeneous Peer Effects
papers.contribution: Proves more robust to complex influence mechanisms than naive GNN approaches, with evaluation on synthetic and semi-synthetic data demonstrating superior performance.

papers.title: Overlap-weighted orthogonal meta-learner for treatment effect estimation over time
papers.contribution: The WO-learner is Neyman-orthogonal (robust to nuisance misspecification), fully model-agnostic, and provides more reliable HTE estimates under low overlap conditions.

papers.title: Query-Specific Causal Graph Pruning Under Tiered Knowledge
papers.contribution: Achieves exponential speedups compared to existing methods when tiered knowledge is available by recovering reduced graphs tailored to specific causal queries.

papers.title: Theoretical Guarantees for Causal Discovery on Large Random Graphs
papers.contribution: Shows FNR concentrates at rate O(log d / sqrt(d)) for ER graphs; demonstrates FNR deviation vanishes for BA graphs with degree exponent γ > 3, indicating heterogeneous networks intrinsically regularize causal discovery.

papers.title: A Minimax Approach for Optimal Intervention Policy Learning with Two-Stage Outcomes
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees for optimal intervention allocation accounting for two-stage outcomes with experimental validation of effectiveness.

papers.title: A Recursive Decomposition Framework for Causal Structure Learning in the Presence of Latent Variables
papers.contribution: DiCoLa significantly improves computational efficiency across causal discovery algorithms while maintaining soundness and completeness.

papers.title: A Relative Error-Based Evaluation Framework of Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimators
papers.contribution: The framework supports reliable comparisons across HTE estimators and the proposed HTE learning algorithm achieves desirable performance through leveraging both prior estimators and learned nuisance parameters.

papers.title: Addressing Instrument-Outcome Confounding in Mendelian Randomization through Representation Learning
papers.contribution: The approach provides theoretical insights into when learned components act as valid instruments and demonstrates effectiveness through simulations and semi-synthetic experiments using the All of Us Biobank.

papers.title: Adjusting Prediction Model Through Wasserstein Geodesic for Causal Inference
papers.contribution: Avoids over-balancing issues and demonstrates effectiveness across benchmark datasets in terms of multiple evaluation metrics with theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Anti-causal domain generalization: Leveraging unlabeled data
papers.contribution: Finally, we demonstrate the empirical performance of our approach on a controlled physical system and a physiological signal dataset

papers.title: Budgeted Active Experimentation for Treatment Effect Estimation from Observational and Randomized Data
papers.contribution: Provides finite-sample deviation bounds, asymptotic normality, and minimax lower bounds showing near-optimality in linear settings with improved sample efficiency.

papers.title: Causal Effect Identifiability in the Presence of Latent Confounders Without Auxiliary Variables
papers.contribution: Establishes equivalence of independent monitoring and non-informative censoring for Case-1 data but not Case-K, and quantifies solution space cardinality for unidentifiable cases.

papers.title: Causal Identification from Counterfactual Data: Completeness and Bounding Results
papers.contribution: Proves which counterfactuals are identifiable from realizable counterfactual data and derives tighter analytic bounds for non-identifiable quantities.

papers.title: Causal Matrix Completion under Multiple Treatments via Mixed Synthetic Nearest Neighbors
papers.contribution: MSNN especially effective under data-scarce treatment levels; demonstrates efficacy on synthetic and real-world datasets.

papers.title: Causal Modeling of Selection in Evolution
papers.contribution: Provides methods to uncover mechanisms underlying evolution from data, avoiding false discovery from conflating selection forms.

papers.title: Causal Preference Elicitation
papers.contribution: Achieves faster posterior concentration and improved recovery of directed causal effects under tight query budgets on synthetic and biological datasets.

papers.title: Causal discovery for time series with endogenous context variables
papers.contribution: Theoretically sound algorithms with proof of correctness; systematic evaluation on benchmarks and land-atmosphere feedback application demonstrates effectiveness.

papers.title: Coarse-to-Fine Learning of Dynamic Causal Structures
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods on synthetic and real-world datasets, effectively identifying fully dynamic causal structures from coarse to fine temporal scales.

papers.title: Conditional Distributional Treatment Effects: Doubly Robust Estimation and Testing
papers.contribution: First test with provably valid type 1 error and consistency against fixed alternatives for global homogeneity of conditional potential outcome distributions.

papers.title: Conditional Independent Component Analysis For Estimating Causal Structure with Latent Variables
papers.contribution: Establishes identifiability theory for linear non-Gaussian acyclic models with latent variables and substantiates with experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets.

papers.title: Conformalized Survival Counterfactuals Prediction for General Right-Censored Data
papers.contribution: Empirical evaluation on synthetic and real-world clinical data demonstrates the validity and informativeness of the constructed lower prediction bounds.

papers.title: Counterfactual Structural Causal Bandits
papers.contribution: The ctf-SCB framework provides a principled extension of structural causal bandits that integrates counterfactual reasoning into sequential decision-making.

papers.title: Dissecting Causal Mechanism Shifts via FANS: Function And Noise Separation
papers.contribution: Extends beyond additive noise models to handle non-additive, non-linear SCMs and addresses simultaneous function-noise shifts with formal identifiability assumptions.

papers.title: Efficient Ensemble Conditional Independence Test Framework for Causal Discovery
papers.contribution: Reduces computational complexity of base CITs to linear in sample size when subset size is fixed, achieving competitive performance while significantly reducing computational burden on causal discovery.

papers.title: Estimating Continuous Treatment Effects with Two-Stage Kernel Ridge Regression
papers.contribution: Achieves optimal learning bounds without estimating conditional treatment density and includes a fully data-driven model selection procedure with provable adaptivity.

papers.title: Estimation of Treatment Effects Under Nonstationarity via the Truncated Policy Gradient Estimator
papers.contribution: Establishes central limit theorem for TPG and develops consistent variance estimator valid under nonstationarity, validated on real-world case studies.

papers.title: Evaluating Bivariate Causal Statements Based on Mutual Compatibility
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical and empirical evidence that compatibility and incompatibility scores distinguish correct from incorrect causal statements, with application to evaluating LLM-generated causal claims.

papers.title: Frequentist Consistency of Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Causal Inference
papers.contribution: Calibrated PFNs produce ATE uncertainty that asymptotically matches frequentist uncertainty and is well-calibrated in finite samples.

papers.title: Gateways to Tractability for Satisfiability in Pearl’s Causal Hierarchy
papers.contribution: Provides first fixed-parameter algorithms with matching hardness results that map the limits of tractability for causal reasoning in Pearl's Causal Hierarchy.

papers.title: Generative Augmented Inference
papers.contribution: Enables consistent estimation with valid inference from combined human and AI data, improving asymptotic efficiency and confidence interval quality.

papers.title: Global Directional Priors with Local Statistical Validation for Scalable Causal Discovery
papers.contribution: Significantly improves precision and robustness in high-dimensional regimes where conventional CI-based approaches fail.

papers.title: Gradient-Based Causal Tree Ensembles: A Backbone Architecture for Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
papers.contribution: Consistently surpasses neural network and tree-based baselines on diverse benchmarks with substantial margins in binary and non-binary treatment settings.

papers.title: Heterogeneous Front-Door Effects: Debiased Estimation with Quasi-Oracle Guarantees
papers.contribution: Both learners achieve fast quasi-oracle convergence rates with robust, debiased heterogeneous treatment effect estimates under front-door scenarios.

papers.title: Identifiable Nonlinear Differentiable Causal Discovery via Independence and Adaptive Group Sparsity
papers.contribution: Achieves effective and stable DAG recovery across diverse noise types and variances, providing identifiability guarantees for nonlinear models with arbitrary noise distributions.

papers.title: Independence Test for Linear Non-Gaussian Data and Applications in Causal Discovery
papers.contribution: Achieves higher statistical power than existing approaches and significantly improves downstream causal discovery performance.

papers.title: Influence without Confounding: Causal Discovery from Temporal Data with Long-term Carry-over Effects
papers.contribution: In static cases reduces SHD by 17.29%-40.00% and improves F1 by 5.30%-8.79% over baselines; in temporal cases achieves 64% reduction.

papers.title: Learning Treatment Representations for Downstream Instrumental Variable Regression
papers.contribution: Ensure identification of optimal outcome-prediction directions with limited instruments, showing significant improvements on large-scale clinical data.

papers.title: Many Experiments, Few Repetitions, Unpaired Data, and Sparse Effects: Is Causal Inference Possible?
papers.contribution: Proves consistency as number of environments grows with constant sample size per environment; extends to sparse causal effects via L1-regularization.

papers.title: Multi-View Causal Discovery without Non-Gaussianity: Identifiability and Algorithms
papers.contribution: Multi-view methods inspired by DirectLiNGAM, PairwiseLiNGAM, and ICA-LiNGAM enable causal graph estimation from neuroimaging data.

papers.title: On the Identifiability of Poisson Branching Structural Causal Model Under Latent Confounding
papers.contribution: The work establishes complete identifiability conditions for local 3-variable causal patterns and proposes a practical algorithm demonstrating effectiveness on synthetic and real-world datasets.

papers.title: On the identifiability of causal graphs with multiple environments
papers.contribution: First result guaranteeing complete causal graph recovery with only a constant number of environments (as few as two) and arbitrary nonlinear mechanisms.

papers.title: Overlap-Adaptive Regularization for Conditional Average Treatment Effect Estimation
papers.contribution: OAR significantly improves CATE estimation in low-overlap settings compared to constant regularization across both parametric and non-parametric meta-learners.

papers.title: PACER: Acyclic Causal Discovery from Large-scale Interventional Data
papers.contribution: PACER matches or exceeds state-of-the-art methods on protein signaling and genetic perturbation benchmarks while scaling to thousands of variables with up to two orders of magnitude speedup.

papers.title: Power-Boosted Granger-Causal Discovery for Large Heterogeneous Panel Data
papers.contribution: Theoretically guarantees asymptotic behavior with negligible size distortion under null and significant power gains under alternatives on high-dimensional and sparse panel data.

papers.title: Rank-Learner: Orthogonal Ranking of Treatment Effects
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms standard CATE estimators and non-orthogonal ranking methods while providing theoretical guarantees including robustness to nuisance function estimation errors.

papers.title: Regret-Based Federated Causal Discovery with Unknown Interventions
papers.contribution: I-PERI provides theoretical convergence guarantees and privacy-preserving properties while recovering causal structure more tightly than assuming homogeneity.

papers.title: ScoreMatchingRiesz: Score Matching for Debiased Machine Learning and Policy Path Estimation
papers.contribution: Stabilizes representer estimation while enabling √n-consistent and asymptotically efficient causal effect estimation with improved interpretability of policy effects.

papers.title: Sinkhorn Treatment Effects: A Causal Optimal Transport Measure
papers.contribution: First-order pathwise differentiability is established in general and second-order pathwise differentiability under the null hypothesis, enabling debiased estimators and asymptotically valid tests.

papers.title: Skewness-Robust Causal Discovery in Location-Scale Noise Models
papers.contribution: Enable reliable causal inference in location-scale noise models under both symmetric and skewed noise, extending beyond bivariate to multivariate cause-effect inference.

papers.title: Stochastic Neural Networks for Causal Inference with Missing Confounders
papers.contribution: CI-StoNet provides state-of-the-art performance on causal effect estimation benchmarks and demonstrates adaptability to proxy variable and multiple-cause scenarios.

papers.title: Test-Time Learning of Causal Structure from Interventional Data
papers.contribution: Superior performance on bnlearn benchmarks for both causal discovery and intervention target detection.

papers.title: The Fisher Dimension: Instance-Dependent Complexity for Causal Discovery
papers.contribution: Empirical validation shows strong correlation between our predictor and observed sample complexity for structured graph families

papers.title: Topological Causal Effects
papers.contribution: Proposes doubly robust estimator with asymptotic properties and formal test for null hypothesis; reliably quantifies treatment effects across diverse outcome spaces.

papers.title: Towards Completeness in Causal Discovery from Soft Interventions with Known Targets
papers.contribution: Theoretically complete causal discovery from soft interventions with known targets under latent confounding.

papers.title: Towards a Holistic Understanding of Selection Bias for Causal Effect Identification
papers.contribution: Offers more comprehensive understanding of causal effect identification with strictly weaker conditions than existing frameworks.

papers.title: Transformers with Endogenous In-Context Learning: Bias Characterization and Mitigation
papers.contribution: The analysis shows pre-trained transformers exhibit prediction bias proportional to confounding strength, and DDbias enables unbiased ICL predictions.

papers.title: Treatment Responder Classification with Abstention
papers.contribution: Learn treatment responder classification rules with low regret and theoretical guarantees under loose convergence conditions on nuisance parameters.

papers.title: Understanding Generalization and Forgetting in In-Context Continual Learning
papers.contribution: This analysis exposes fundamental limits of attention-based continual inference and offers theoretical explanations for order sensitivity and performance degradation in long prompts..

papers.title: Unveiling Prior-Data Fitted Networks on Causal Effect Estimation: Pre-Training or Fine-Tuning?
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that fine-tuning is necessary to achieve posterior consistency and local generalization properties in causal effect estimation.

papers.title: Unveiling the Structure of Do-Calculus Reasoning via Derivation Graphs
papers.contribution: Provides efficient procedure for do-calculus reasoning and shows how identification algorithms applied to equivalent queries produce multiple valid estimands for more efficient estimation.

papers.title: Use What You Know: Causal Foundation Models with Partial Graphs
papers.contribution: Allows general-purpose CFMs to match performance of specialized models trained on specific causal structures while maintaining flexibility.

papers.title: When Shift Happens - Confounding Is to Blame
papers.contribution: Proves that models augmented with non-causal but informative covariates can mitigate challenges from hidden confounding shifts.
